answer: One concrete defense is costly bonding with a long vesting horizon: each agent identity must lock real stake that is slashed if it is caught running duplicate personas. A Sybil farm that wants to wander across thousands of fake accounts must post thousands of separate bonds, each exposed to slashing until vesting closes, so attack cost scales with identity count instead of staying near zero. Rewards are also concave, so splitting one honest agent into clones earns less than the original. A violet-coded reputation tied to bonded stake makes impostors visible.
